content: Ceftaroline is indicated for the treatment of community-acquired bacterial pneumonia (CABP) in adults at a dosage of 600 mg administered intravenously every 12 hours for 5 to 7 days. For acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (ABSSSI), including those caused by MRSA, the recommended dosage is 600 mg intravenously every 12 hours for 5 to 14 days. In pediatric patients aged ≥2 months, ceftaroline is indicated for the treatment of CABP. For children aged 2 months to <2 years, the dosage is 8 mg/kg intravenously every 8 hours for 5 to 14 days. For children aged ≥2 years to <18 years weighing ≤33 kg, the dosage is 12 mg/kg intravenously every 8 hours for 5 to 14 days. For children aged ≥2 years to <18 years weighing >33 kg, the dosage is either 400 mg intravenously every 8 hours or 600 mg intravenously every 12 hours for 5 to 14 days. For adults aged ≥18 years, the dosage is 600 mg intravenously every 12 hours for 5 to 7 days. Ceftaroline is also indicated for the treatment of ABSSSI in pediatric patients, including neonates born at ≥34 weeks of gestation and at least 12 days postnatal age. For neonates from birth to <2 months, the dosage is 6 mg/kg intravenously every 8 hours for 5 to 14 days. For children aged 2 months to <2 years, the dosage is 8 mg/kg intravenously every 8 hours for 5 to 14 days. For children aged ≥2 years to <18 years weighing ≤33 kg, the dosage is 12 mg/kg intravenously every 8 hours for 5 to 14 days. For children aged ≥2 years to <18 years weighing >33 kg, the dosage is either 400 mg intravenously every 8 hours or 600 mg intravenously every 12 hours for 5 to 14 days. For adults aged ≥18 years, the dosage is 600 mg intravenously every 12 hours for 5 to 14 days. Ceftaroline decreases the effects of BCG intravesical live vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated, and vaccination should be delayed until antibiotic treatment is completed. Ceftaroline decreases the effects of the live typhoid vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. The vaccine should be administered either 3 days before starting antibiotics or 3 days after completing the antibiotic course. Ceftaroline interacts with the cholera vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Co-administration with systemic antibiotics should be avoided, as these agents may act against the vaccine strain. The cholera vaccine should not be administered to patients who have received oral or parenteral antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. Ceftaroline decreases the effects of oral microbiota products due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. These products contain bacterial spores, and co-administration with antibacterial agents may reduce their efficacy. Antibiotic regimens should be completed 2 to 4 days before initiating oral microbiota therapy. Ceftaroline increases the toxicity of aminoglycosides such as amikacin, gentamicin, kanamycin, neomycin, streptomycin, and tobramycin through nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Caution should be exercised, and patients should be closely monitored. Cephalosporins may enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. Ceftaroline decreases the effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors, including atezolizumab, avelumab, balstilimab, camrelizumab, cemiplimab, cosibelimab, dostarlimab, durvalumab, nivolumab, pembrolizumab, penpulimab, retifanlimab, sintilimab, and tislelizumab, through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Co-administration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of these agents. Caution should be exercised, and patients should be closely monitored. Ceftaroline increases the effects of warfarin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution should be exercised, and patients should be monitored for potential changes in anticoagulant effects. Ceftaroline increases the effects of antithrombin III, fondaparinux, pentosan polysulfate sodium, reteplase, and tenecteplase through mechanisms associated with cephalosporins containing a methylthiotetrazole (MTT) side ring. These agents are more frequently associated with hypoprothrombinemic activity. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown, but caution is advised. Ceftaroline increases the levels of ceftaroline itself when co-administered with probenecid due to competition for renal tubular clearance. Caution should be exercised, and patients should be monitored. Ceftaroline decreases the effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering colonic bacterial flora, which is necessary for converting sodium picosulfate into its active form. Caution should be exercised, and the efficacy of this combination should be monitored. Ceftaroline increases the effects of alteplase through mechanisms associated with cephalosporins containing an MTT side ring. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but caution is advised.
